notes.title: The Ghosts We Need
notes.descriptor: You cannot see your own story from inside it. Why leaders need someone allowed to interrupt them.
notes.summary: Scrooge did not change by trying harder. Leaders turn people into roles without noticing, and we cannot see it from inside. Three kinds of interruption a leader can build in.

notes.title: The Cleaning Station
notes.descriptor: Even the biggest fish on the reef cannot see its own gills. Why leaders need someone to read their receipts with them.
notes.summary: Most leaders believe they see themselves clearly, and the higher they rise, the fewer people will tell them otherwise. What coaching is for, and a receipts review you can start this month.

notes.title: Who Else Knows How?
notes.descriptor: A forty-five-minute exercise that turns your next staff meeting from reporting into tracing.
notes.summary: You cannot find where the delivery lives on your own. Your crew already knows. A meeting plan for finding out together.

notes.title: The One Who Tried to Change Everything
notes.descriptor: When a beloved leader leaves, the next one often takes the blame. The better question is where the delivery lived.
notes.summary: Charisma carries the day, and so does tradition. Neither transfers. Why successors get blamed, and what a leader can build before leaving.

notes.title: The Junco and the Fire Engine
notes.descriptor: What two alarms in one neighborhood teach us about the stories we tell
notes.summary: A bird that sounds like a car alarm and a siren with responders on the way. One story lands. The other one works.

notes.title: The Windmill and the Ask
notes.descriptor: On wind turbines, car lots, and standing where the wind already blows
notes.summary: A wind turbine does not make the wind. A good ask does not make the donor’s motivation either. It stands where that motivation already moves.

notes.title: The Second Draw
notes.descriptor: On a repeated blood test, a two-hour wait, and the person standing in the gap
notes.summary: Two blood draws, two hours apart, looked redundant. They were the only way to know nothing was happening, and someone made room to find out.

notes.title: The Most Skeptical Donors Gave the Most
notes.descriptor: A headline said connection beats trust. The study underneath it said something more useful.
notes.summary: A headline said connection beats trust. The donors who trusted charities least gave the most, and that tells us which trust matters.

notes.title: Who Did It Bring Together?
notes.descriptor: On nostalgia, inefficient events, and the flock an affinity makes visible for a day
notes.summary: A car show and an air show are poor fundraisers. Their real yield is the community they gather, a crowd of strangers who turn out to be a flock.

notes.title: A Jay in My Yard
notes.descriptor: On love for one person, the gift you never reclaim, and keeping the ground open
notes.summary: A backyard jay buries acorns to survive one winter and, without meaning to, plants the forest that outlives her.

notes.title: Planting on Purpose
notes.descriptor: A major gifts program that starts at the first gift, not the wealth screen
notes.summary: The napkin asked what’s being planted now. This is the answer: a major gifts program that begins at the first gift.

notes.title: What’s Being Planted Now?
notes.descriptor: Giving USA announced a record year. I drew a pyramid on a napkin.
notes.summary: A record fundraising year is a harvest planted a decade ago. The question the napkin asks is what’s being planted now.

notes.title: They Know the River
notes.descriptor: What salmon can teach us about the loop fundraising runs
notes.summary: Marcus fixed the late card. He never fixed the system that produced it. A field note on single-loop learning, told through the salmon run.

notes.title: What a Room Can’t Trace
notes.descriptor: A story about the question fundraising never learned to ask
notes.summary: Every experienced fundraiser can name a failed receipt in sixty seconds. Ask them to trace it to its cause, and the room goes quiet.
